text.p: The chief executive officer of Porsche AG said on Tuesday he expected it to at least double the first half profit of 38.4 million marks reported for the 1996/97 business year.
"I think you can at least double the first half profit," Porsche chief executive Wendelin Wiedeking told Reuters in an interview at the Geneva car show. "That's something you can measure us on."

The German sports car maker said last Friday that first-half net profit nearly quadrupled to 38.4 million marks, led by robust demand for the new Boxster roadster model and the continued popularity of the 911, the only two cars produced by the Stuttgart carmaker.
Porsche reported a net profit of 48.0 million marks for the 1995/96 business year.

The carmaker has seen dramatic sales growth for the two-seat Boxster cabriolet, which was first introduced last autumn. Porsche's plant in Stuttgart, which has a capacity of about 30,000 cars a year, cannot keep up with deamnd which now has an order backlog of about a year.
Porsche said in January that it has signed a deal with Finland's Valmet Oy to assemble some of the Boxsters after Porsche decided not to expand German-based production.
